HTTP/2 connection state, frame receive handling, and control frame transmit logic.

# Purpose
This C file implements the core connection logic for an HTTP/2 endpoint. It defines client and server connection initialization, default local and peer settings, flow-control window setup, and the client connection preface and initial `SETTINGS` frame generation. It also provides the main receive and transmit control paths for a connection, including frame parsing, frame dispatch, and generation of control frames such as `SETTINGS`, `PING`, `GOAWAY`, and `WINDOW_UPDATE`.

The receive path handles HTTP/2 frame types such as `DATA`, `HEADERS`, `CONTINUATION`, `RST_STREAM`, `SETTINGS`, `PING`, `GOAWAY`, and `WINDOW_UPDATE`. It validates frame size, stream state, stream ordering, padding, and flow-control limits, then calls callback functions to notify the application about headers, data, stream resets, window updates, connection establishment, and connection final state. The file uses `fd_h2_conn_t`, `fd_h2_stream_t`, and ring buffers to manage connection state and buffered I/O, so it acts as the main protocol engine for HTTP/2 connection processing.
